newsitem.title: USA: Low US winter wheat may prompt more spring wheat.
newsitem.headline: Low US winter wheat may prompt more spring wheat.

text.p: Low U.S. winter wheat seedings could prompt more plantings later this year of spring wheat, said Agriculture Department officials Friday shortly after the release of USDA's Winter Wheat Seedings report.
"This is just winter wheat seedings...a lot of times when you see low winter wheat, you see more spring wheat plantings to fill in the void," said Ray Halley, chief of USDA's crop branch.
Halley noted, however, that farmers have unprecedented planting flexibility this year due to the new farm bill, which makes any speculation on future plantings even more uncertain than ever.
USDA estimated winter wheat plantings at 48.2 million acres, down seven percent from last year and the lowest planted acreage since 1978.
Fred Vogel, director of USDA's estimates division, said, "It is a safe assumption" that more non-wheat crops will be planted this year because of the new farm bill. reuter
